To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) M-PAM with minimum mean-square-error decision-feedback equalization is the optimal choice for indoor optical wireless communications at low spectral efficiency; (2) DC-OFDM and ACO-OFDEM have similar performance at low spectral efficiency but DC-OFDM outperforms ACO-OFDE at high spectral efficiency; and (3) ACO-OFEM and PAM-DEMT are the best OFEM formats when they are allowed to use the same bandwidth and symbol rate

M-PAM with minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) decision-feedback equalization is superior to any orthogonal frequency-division-multiplexing (OFM) format in combating multipath in indoor optical wireless channels when channel state information is not available at the transmitter.

M-PAM with minimum-mean-square-error decision-feedback equalization outperforms all orthogonal frequency-division-multiplexing formats, except at very high bit rates, where asymmetrically clipped optical orthogonal frequency-divisionmultiplexing and PAM-modulation discrete multitone are the best formats, and that M-PAM is significantly less computationally complex than any orthogonal frequency-division- multiplexing format.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of three OFDM schemes in indoor optical wireless channels.
the performance and complexity comparison of M-PAM with three OFDM formats in indoor optical wireless systems.
the performance of OFDM and M-P AM in indoor optical wireless systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OFDM is a viable modulation format for indoor optical wireless communications, especially when the symbol rate is increased to twice that of M-PAM.

OFDM is the best modulation format for indoor optical wireless links at high data rates, but that M-PAM is the best modulation for indoor optical wireless at lower data rates, where channel state information is not available.
M-PAM is the best modulation method for indoor optical wireless links at low spectral efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in indoor wireless optical channels, M-PAM has better performance than all OFDM methods when using the same symbol rates, and OFDM methods have better performance than unipolar M-PAM when using twice the symbol rates.
OFDM formats can provide a significant performance advantage over M-PAM when using twice the symbol rate, but when channel state information is unknown at the transmitter, M-PAM is a better choice.
OFDM is the best modulation format for indoor optical wireless systems at low spectral efficiency and M-PAM is best at high efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for indoor wireless channels with significant multipath distortion, OFDM formats are superior to M-PAM when channel state information is available at the transmitter, but M-PAM with equalization is superior to OFDM when channel state information unavailable at the transmitter.
OFDM is the preferred modulation method for indoor optical wireless links.
M-PAM with equalization is a good choice for indoor optical wireless communications when the channel is not known at the transmitter.
